text: Your sect grants you a day in its Scripture Pavilion. You may study one art.

outcomes.text: Weeks of drills harden your body.
The words settle your thoughts like still water.
You practice until leaves no longer rustle beneath your feet.

text: A traveling master studies you for a long moment. 'Your root has a natural voice,' he says. 'Let me teach you an art that sings with it.'

outcomes.text: He teaches you to wrap your palms in true flame.
He teaches you to let your qi flow like a river.
He teaches you to draw life from the green world.
He teaches you a sword intent of cold, clean edges.
He teaches you to stand firm as bedrock.
He pauses, awed. 'A Heavenly root. I have only the oldest art to give you.'
He bows and wanders on. The chance does not return.

text: Behind a collapsed wall you find a sealed library. Its door hums with a protective formation.

outcomes.text: The formation yields. Among the dusty scrolls you find an art of perfect stillness.
The seal's guardian drives you out, bruised.
Some doors are better left closed.

text: A mountain peak crackles with endless lightning. Old texts say an art lies buried in its heart.

outcomes.text: Lightning writes its own art across your meridians.
The storm throws you down the slope.

text: In a hidden grove a single red-gold feather drifts down, warm as a hearth. A phoenix once nested here.

outcomes.text: You wake with its memory in your bones: an art of flame and renewal.
The feather's fire turns on you.
You let the grove keep its secret.
